title: Ingest deduplication, scrub & enrichment for Loki-backed aggregation
creator: Ava Chen
description: Build a two-stage log ingestion pipeline for structured events that reduces duplicate writes, strips PII, and enriches records with service/zone metadata before they land in Loki. The pipeline will operate at the edge ingress and at the Kafka consumer side to balance latency and durability. Goals: 80% reduction in duplicate events, maintain sub-150ms ingest processing latency at p50, and ensure sensitive fields are removed per compliance rules.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Stateful dedup works across a 30s sliding window and reduces duplicate writes to Loki by >=80% in k6 load tests; 2) PII scrub rules remove email/SSN-like patterns from event payloads and are configurable via Confluence-managed regex list; 3) Enrichment adds service_name, zone, and tenant labels consistently and these labels appear in Loki/Grafana queries; 4) End-to-end pipeline introduces <5% additional CPU at peak on current demo nodes; 5) Rollout can be gated per-tenant with feature-flag and has a canary plan documented.
design_decisions: 1) Two-stage approach: lightweight fingerprinting at edge (Fluent Bit plugin) and authoritative dedup at consumer using compacted Kafka or Redis state store depending on tenant SLA; trade-off: edge reduces wasted upstream I/O but can't be authoritative on retries; consumer dedup ensures single-write guarantee for high-SLA tenants. 2) Use JSON-structured logs as canonical format; single adapter converts legacy text logs to the schema to avoid multiple downstream consumers. 3) PII scrubbing performed before enrichment to avoid accidental label leakage; implemented as a streaming scrubber with a safe allowlist. 4) Use Loki labels for high-cardinality fields only for a bounded set (service, zone, env) and attach other metadata into the JSON payload to avoid index blowup. 5) Backpressure: if dedup store (Redis) is saturated, auto-fallback to sampling mode and emit telemetry metric and alert.
implementation_plan: Prototype Fluent Bit fingerprinting plugin (edge) and validate on staging with demo traffic
Implement consumer-side dedup service (Go) with Redis TTL window and Kafka compacted fallback
Integrate JSON scrubber and make regex rules configurable via Confluence + infra repo
Add enrichment layer pulling service metadata from service-registry and cache locally
Add feature-flag gating and per-tenant rollout controls in deployment manifests
End-to-end load test with k6 and record duplicate rates, latencies, CPU/mem profiles
Dashboarding: Grafana panels for duplicate_rate, scrubbed_events, dedup_latency, fallback_count
Docs: runbook + rollout checklist + SLO update
progress_updates: 2026-02-12: Triage complete; scoping doc created (Confluence link below). Assigned to Diego Ruiz.
2026-02-20: Spike finished — Fluent Bit prototype computes stable fingerprint and emits 'fingerprint' label. Prototype PR opened (github.com/redwood/obs/pull/812).
2026-02-28: Consumer dedup service skeleton merged to feature branch (github.com/redwood/obs/pull/829). Decided to back Redis with optional Kafka-compacted table for high-volume tenants.
2026-03-05: Security reviewed regex scrubber approach; recommended allowlist and denylist staging toggles. Security team requested a QA plan to prove no false negatives on sample data.
2026-03-10: Load test scheduled for 2026-03-15; added temporary metrics to collect duplicate_count and scrub_errors. Canary rollout plan drafted.
2026-03-12: Implemented initial Grafana panels and alerts; working through flaky tests in consumer dedup's Redis integration.
review_feedback: PM (Jordan Patel): prefer conservative rollout by tenant and metric gated; Design (Maya Singh): prefer moving enrichments to consumer to avoid retry-amplification; Security (Lars Becker): require snapshot tests for scrubber with real examples before deploy.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Redis TTL store could grow unexpectedly under bursty traffic. Mitigation: enforce max keys per-tenant; auto-switch to sampling + alert. Risk: False positives by scrub regex could drop legitimate data. Mitigation: run scrubber in dry-run mode for 48h and capture examples, then iterate rules.
qa_notes: QA should run k6 scenario with synthetic duplicate injection at 2x production rate, validate Grafana duplicate_rate drops by target, confirm scrubbed fields absent in Loki entries, and verify labels for service/zone present on queries. Include tenant gating tests where consumer falls back to sampling.
